tally.headline: 1 of 11 gradeable claims held up, 2 did not

implied_side.why: EdgeDesk’s own number sat 3.7 points toward Green Bay Packers of the quote EdgeDesk captured at FanDuel. That is what the disagreement implied. It was published as research, not as a recommendation to bet it.

implied_total.why: EdgeDesk’s fair total of 50.3 sat 0.2 points below the captured total of 50.5.

closing_line.note: The line moved 2.8 points toward the side EdgeDesk’s number leaned before kickoff. That is the market arriving where EdgeDesk already was, and over many games it is the only evidence that a disagreement carried information.

reasons: 0 claims held up, 7 held up in direction only and 2 did not. Parts of the read were right and parts were not.
EdgeDesk projected a home margin of 2.2 and the game finished 10 the home way — 7.8 points of margin error, inside the range the model published.
process.basis: the drivers, matchups and measured advantages only — never the price or the market claim, which are the result in longer words

verdict.line: The number landed, and some of the reasoning behind it held up. Take the result; do not take it as confirmation of the parts that did not.

grading.separation_note: The bet result and the process grade above are computed separately and are allowed to disagree. A winning number with a broken thesis is recorded as exactly that.

lessons.pregame_expectation: Points scored and allowed, opponent-adjusted — Dallas Cowboys by 1.4 points — worth -1.4 of the EdgeDesk number, in Dallas Cowboys’s favour.
lessons.actual_result: Dallas Cowboys 13 points against Green Bay Packers 23.
lessons.lesson: EdgeDesk named Dallas Cowboys as better in scoring and the game went the other way. One game does not overturn a season-long rating, but this is the direction to watch: every signal this claim rests on went the other way

lessons.pregame_expectation: Dallas Cowboys’ pass offence rates +0.115 (#8 of 32) and Green Bay Packers’ pass defence rates +0.081 (#24 of 32). Added the way the model adds them, this pairing sits +0.195 from the league mean, which favours Dallas Cowboys.
lessons.actual_result: Dallas Cowboys 4.64 yards per pass attempt against Green Bay Packers 5.93; Dallas Cowboys 255 net passing yards against Green Bay Packers 261.
lessons.lesson: EdgeDesk named Dallas Cowboys as better in passing and the game went the other way. One game does not overturn a season-long rating, but this is the direction to watch: every signal this claim rests on went the other way
lessons.suggested_investigation: These claims carried 2 points of the published number between them and were contradicted. Check whether the same category has been contradicted in other games this season before touching anything.

lessons.pregame_expectation: 1 of the claims in this article rested on model.
lessons.actual_result: None of them could be graded: no single-game statistic in EdgeDesk’s vocabulary observes this driver.
lessons.lesson: EdgeDesk prices these games partly on signals it has no way to observe afterwards. That is not an error in the model — it is a gap in the audit, and it means the platform cannot tell, from results alone, whether those parts of the number are earning their weight.
lessons.suggested_investigation: Consider whether a postgame data source exists for model.

lessons.pregame_expectation: EdgeDesk published a fair total of 50.3.
lessons.actual_result: The game finished with 36 points, an error of 14.3.
lessons.lesson: A total missed by this much usually means a pace or a finishing assumption was wrong, not that both ratings were. Check which of the two moved.
lessons.suggested_investigation: Was the play count or the points per drive the miss? Both are in this game’s result record.

lessons.pregame_expectation: EdgeDesk makes it Green Bay Packers −2.0 where the market has Green Bay Packers +1.5 at FanDuel — a 3.7 points disagreement.
lessons.actual_result: Green Bay Packers won by 10. the result landed on EdgeDesk’s side of the market number: Green Bay Packers beat a margin of -1.5
lessons.lesson: The disagreement landed. One landing proves nothing on its own; the aggregate of them, held against the closing line, is the only thing that would.
